findings.problem: Prose says the sanitizer is 'exported from the web resolver and reused by the controller logic'; apps/api cannot import apps/web, so that cross-app import is not possible. The concrete snippets already inline the logic correctly.
findings.fix: Reword: the per-section sanitize logic is implemented in both the web resolver and the public controller; the only shared artifact is homeSectionSchema imported from @belzo/shared in each.

findings.problem: homeSectionsSchema has no .min(1), so an admin can save []. On read, valid.length===0 returns null which triggers DEFAULT_SECTIONS, so an intentionally-emptied config silently reverts to the three default rails.
findings.fix: Document that an empty saved array is treated as unconfigured and falls back to defaults; to render no rails, disable all sections (enabled:false) rather than deleting them.

findings.problem: The composition of getHomeSections (applies defaults + filters enabled) and resolveHomeSections is implied but never shown as a single call, risking an unfiltered/undefaulted list being resolved.
findings.fix: Show the concrete call once: const sections = await resolveHomeSections(await getHomeSections()); in both page.tsx and emart-home.tsx.

findings.problem: 'No extra round-trip' depends on Next.js fetch request memoization requiring identical URL AND options; a differing revalidate/options shape in getHomeSections would cause a second request to /settings/public.
findings.fix: Require getHomeSections to use the exact same apiFetch('/settings/public', { revalidate: 30 }) options as getTheme/getSiteContent, or have getSiteContent return sections for getHomeSections to consume.
